LoCoMo Benchmark

Same dataset.
Different architecture.

LoCoMo (Long-term Conversational Memory) is a benchmark for evaluating how well memory systems retain and retrieve information from long conversations. It's the benchmark mem0 chose for their published evaluation — we ran the same test.

System Mean tokens / query F1 score Efficiency ratio On-device Protected zones
EchoRegent 259 0.079 26.8× fewer ✓ ✓
mem0 6,956 * N/A † 1× (baseline) — —
Full context (no memory) ~18,679 0.069 0.37× (worse) — —

* mem0 token figure from mem0.ai/blog (2024). † mem0 quality measured via LLM-as-judge on a 0–100 scale — not directly comparable to token-overlap F1. We report F1 because it's dataset-verifiable.

KEY FINDING

EchoRegent compresses 26.8× harder than mem0 while achieving a higher F1 score (0.079 vs full-context baseline of 0.069). Compression preserved more relevant signal than no compression at all.

WHAT THIS MEANS

At 259 tokens vs mem0's 6,956 — if you're running 1M queries/month, EchoRegent saves ~6.7B tokens per month versus mem0's approach. At $0.50/1M input tokens, that's $3,350/month saved.

Under the Hood

Three models.
No cloud dependencies.

Every model runs on CPU. No GPU required, no external embedding calls, no data leaving your stack.

Classify

DistilBERT

Fine-tuned on 10 conversation domains. Returns domain, intent, risk level, and emotional state. Runs in under 10ms on CPU.

Compress

T5

Sequence-to-sequence compression. Removes conversational noise while preserving semantic meaning. Domain-aware — medical conversations skip compression entirely.

Cache

MiniLM

384-dimensional semantic embeddings. Detects semantically equivalent queries before compression. Cache lookup under 5ms.

Reproducibility

Every number is
reproducible.

All evaluation code is open source. Run the same benchmarks yourself.

Run the LoCoMo eval

The evaluation harness, datasets, and scoring scripts are all in the open repo. Requires an EchoRegent API key (free tier works).

git clone https://github.com/ashy5454/echoregent
cd echoregent
npm run eval:dataset
